blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why your family buys certain things and not others? Let's explore why some items are essential while others are just nice to have.

blocks.markdown: In our daily lives, we often make decisions about what to buy. These decisions are influenced by our needs and wants. Understanding the difference between these two concepts is crucial for making wise choices.

blocks.title: Needs vs Wants
blocks.text: Needs are essential items required for survival, such as food, water, and shelter. Wants are non-essential items that we desire, like toys or a new smartphone.

blocks.markdown: A family must prioritize needs over wants due to limited resources. Money, which we use to buy goods and services, plays a central role in these decisions. Let's understand how money functions in our economy.

blocks.title: Distinguishing Needs from Wants
blocks.prompt: Consider the following items: rice, a television, school uniform, and a bicycle. Identify which are needs and which are wants for a typical family.

steps.text: Identify essential items for survival or daily living.
Categorize the items: Rice and school uniform are needs, while a television and bicycle are wants.

blocks.answer: Rice and school uniform are needs; television and bicycle are wants.

blocks.markdown: Money serves several functions in our economy. It acts as a medium of exchange, allowing us to trade goods and services. It also serves as a store of value, enabling us to save for future needs or wants.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When distinguishing between needs and wants, ask yourself if the item is essential for daily living or survival.

points: Needs are essential for survival, while wants are additional desires.
Money functions as a medium of exchange and a store of value.
